newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end lower after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end lower after recent gains.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended weak on Tuesday as prices bumped against resistance following recent gains and concerns about higher interest rates prompted some caution, analysts said.
The Hang Seng Index closed 45.19 points, or 0.36 percent, lower at 12,580.85 after falling to 12,533.73 during the session. Turnover was HK$8.73 billion compared with HK$8.06 billion on Monday.
"We did have a good bounce last week but rallies or recoveries can't go up every day," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage.

Brokers said comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve Board vice chairman Alice Rivlin had sparked some concern about higher interest rates. Rivlin said in a speech to the Employment Policy Foundation on Monday that the major threat to the U.S. economy at the moment was the possibility of overheating.
Brokers said some investors saw this as a sign that interest rates were heading higher.
"The market will consolidate further before we see an uptrend because of the interest rate uncertainty," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
He saw the Hang Seng Index trading in a range of 12,300 to 12,700 points for the rest of the week.

Gorges said investors would be watching the property market closely to see how government measures to curb escalating prices were impacting the market. "Until the property sector performs better, the whole Hang Seng Index can't run away," he said.
Gorges said the blue chip barometer was meeting resistance around 12,600 points. "It will still be a little bit sideways," he said of the performance for the remainder of the week.
"It would not suprise me if we did push up higher but I don't think it is going to run away on the upside."
Shares in the property sector were soft.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.25 to HK$68.00 and New World Development Co Ltd lost HK$0.60 to close at HK$40.80. Swire Pacific Ltd dropped HK$1.25 to HK$57.00.

Silver Grant International Industries Ltd rose HK$0.025 to HK$3.95. The company said on Tuesday it planned to raise net proceeds of HK$480 million through the placement of 130.72 million new shares to controlling shareholder Join Truth Ltd.
April Hang Seng Index futures fell 55 points to 12,570.
